patch.value: Reuse unaffected fragments across an edit with content-defined chunking

The fragment path chunks at a fixed size, so inserting bytes near the start of a file shifts every subsequent boundary and re-stores every fragment. Content-defined chunking picks boundaries from the content itself, so an edit re-stores only the fragments it actually touched. Both modes need to coexist: fixed chunks are what make a byte-range read cheap, because the fragment covering an offset is computable rather than searched.

Inserting bytes into a large file re-stores only the fragments overlapping the edit, asserted by counting object files on disk before and after rather than by a reported statistic; fixed-size chunking remains available and range reads over it stay O(fragments in range); the chosen mode is recorded in the manifest so a reader does not have to infer it
